newsitem.title: USA: GFOA panels adopt raft of financial policies.
newsitem.headline: GFOA panels adopt raft of financial policies.

text.p: GFOA panels adopted a series of policies and recommended practices on Saturday dealing with securitizing property tax liens, issuing taxable debt, using variable rate debt instruments and other issues.

The statements, which were adopted by Government Finance Officers Association's governmental debt and cash management panels, are expected to win the approval of the association's executive board on Monday. GFOA's general membership, which is meeting here for its annual convention, will vote on Tuesday.
Another draft practice urges localities to develop a "thorough understanding" of differences between tax-exempt and taxable markets before moving ahead with a taxable bond sale.

"Allow sufficient time to educate potential investors, who may be less familiar with governmental issuers," the draft says. "Consider features that can lower interest costs, such as amortizing debt as quickly as possible or embedding early call provisions."

Another draft practice says that variable rate debt can help lower borrowing costs and offers a hedge against interest rate risk. At the same time, issuers should fully understand variable debt's "unique risks," such as when payments are realized through interest rate swaps that can involve counterparty risks.

A fourth proposal urges legislators to repeal laws that artificially restrict investment of public funds in U.S. government obligations, Canadian bonds, certificates of deposit, top rated commercial paper, some repurchase agreements, some money market mutual funds and top rated state and local obligations.
Investments in derivatives, however, should be authorized by an appropriate governing authority, the proposal says.
Another recommended practice urges governments to save money on routine banking services by periodically initiating competitive bidding from financial institutions for their business.
